subject: Post-call: Model fit & structured-output evals for AveryAnalytics
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam@averyanalytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T17:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Model fit & structured-output evals for AveryAnalytics

Thanks again for the call earlier - really useful. Quick recap and asks so we can align on next steps:

- Goal: Evaluate model candidates and tool/function-calling reliability to support AveryAnalytics' automated reporting product (high-precision JSON outputs consumed by downstream ETL).
- Key success criteria: JSON schema compliance (strict), <1% field-level regression vs baseline, deterministic retries for failed function calls, and end-to-end latency under 500ms p50 for common routes.

Requests from our side:
1) Your recommended model(s) and why (cost vs quality tradeoffs).
2) Example benchmark links and an initial prompt set we can test.
3) Plan for tool/function-calling tests (retries, idempotency checks) and structured-output validation (schema tests).
4) Rough timeline + any costs for a scoped eval.

I attached our initial prompt set (avery_prompt_set_v1.json) used in the call. Can you confirm you have what you need to start a scoped eval?

Thanks - Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Product, AveryAnalytics
sam@averyanalytics.com

--
Attachment: avery_prompt_set_v1.json (application/json)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam@averyanalytics.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T19:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: Model fit & structured-output evals for AveryAnalytics

Hi Sam - great speaking with you and the team. Appreciate the clear success criteria. High-level answers and proposed plan below; happy to sync if you'd like to walk through details.

Recommended models (initial shortlist):
- redwood-longform-v1: best-in-class prompt adherence and structured output; slightly higher token cost but far fewer schema violations in our tests.
- open-llama-13b-quant: cost-efficient alternative for high-throughput routes; performs well on deterministic function-calls but needs prompt engineering to meet strict schema constraints.

Why these two: redwood-longform-v1 minimizes field-level regressions out of the box; the 13b quant variant gives a strong cost vs throughput point if you plan to run large-scale evals. We'll provide per-route perf and token-cost estimates as part of the scoped eval.

Proposed scoped eval (2 weeks):
1) Week 1: Run baseline benchmarks against your prompt set (you sent avery_prompt_set_v1.json) - measure schema pass rate, per-field error, and function-call success/timeout distribution.
2) Week 2: Iterate on prompts and run tool/function-calling tests (retries, idempotency, backoff). We'll include structured-output validators to assert JSON schema compliance and generate a regression matrix vs your baseline.

Deliverables:
- Benchmark report (per-model): schema pass rate, per-field regressions, latency percentiles, and cost estimate.
- Prompt adjustments and a recommended prompt set tuned for schema compliance.
- Tool-calling test harness results (retry behavior, recommended retry/backoff config).
- Concrete next-step proposal for a pilot (timeline + estimated cost).

Attachments I will include in the eval kickoff: redwood_model_recs.pdf (summary + perf profile) and schema_example.json (validator example).

Links for reference: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-avery-benchmarks and https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/averyanalytics-model-fit-2027

Does that plan work? If yes, we'll provision a scoped eval and share a calendar invite for a 30-min kickoff.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference
